upgrade_window.policy: single-hop upgrade from an explicitly supported AND tested released baseline; two MINOR releases of deprecation notice before a removal; the staged intermediate boundaries of #1180 honoured; no promise of a direct upgrade from an unverified historical checkout
upgrade_window.recorded_by: Q5 of #1578 - Accepted: A, qualified, on 2026-11-25 (#1578 comment 7171857760, recorded via scripts/decisions; policy text: docs/architecture/decisions/ADR-0002-semantic-versioning-and-release-baseline-policy.md, section 5)
upgrade_window.supported_baselines: named by 'oldest_supported_baseline' plus every release published after it; the list becomes a released set only when a tag exists (Q1 of #1578: first published tag v0.2.0)
upgrade_window.verification: the oldest supported baseline is actually upgraded from before the FIRST stable publication - #1800 owns that verification; a recorded answer is not a verification
upgrade_window.measured: 0 tags and 0 releases exist (measured_by below), so today the supported set is empty by measurement rather than by omission: there is no baseline to claim yet, and nothing an operator could upgrade from

oldest_supported_baseline: the release carrying #1178 and #1179 - the intermediate release of #1180 answer 3
marker_how_to_read: a deployment is only allowed to upgrade to a #1180-or-later release when django_migrations records the marker; without it, stop at the intermediate release first - migrate alone will NOT warn (#1180)
protected_nodes_why: the names are load-bearing while the bodies are empty: registry/0014, registry/0020 and registry/0037 parent on notify 0005, and 0007 parents on 0006 - a node whose parent is gone fails the whole graph, so #1180 kept the names and emptied the contents
retired_apps_why: the package was removed by #1180; no migration dependency and no INSTALLED_APPS entry may name it as a Django application again (the guarded raw-SQL reads of its orphaned legacy tables inside notify/0006 are legitimate D03 evidence and are not hits)
